stage_vocabulary.SPEC: Reverified and specced in its WI doc. Nothing run.
stage_vocabulary.MEASURED: Fix applied and its acceptance numbers exist; the orchestrator has not yet re-run the doc's definition of done.
stage_vocabulary.LANDED: Definition of done re-run by the orchestrator and passing, in the working tree. Committing or publishing is the user's call and is not part of the stage.
stage_vocabulary.BLOCKED: Waiting on an open decision, or on a dependency that has hit a problem. Plain unmet dependencies are not BLOCKED - dependency order already handles those.
stage_vocabulary.CLOSED: Terminal, with reason recorded (won't fix / superseded). Do not re-open without new evidence named in the reason.

model_vocabulary.fable-5.1: claude-fable-5-1. Novel statistical construction where a wrong derivation is expensive and hard to detect from the output - estimators, identification arguments, inference machinery. Reach for it when the failure mode is a plausible-looking number, not an error.
model_vocabulary.opus-5: claude-opus-5. The default. Anything that makes a ruling, designs an aggregation, moves the feature contract, or turns a measurement into a claim.
model_vocabulary.sonnet-5: claude-sonnet-5. The method is already written down and the judgment call is made - ingest, enumeration, a named refit, a declared schema note. Step back up to opus-5 the moment the leaf doc leaves a choice open.
model_vocabulary.haiku-4-5: claude-haiku-4-5. Throughput work with a mechanical check on the output. Nothing in the tree currently qualifies: every live item either writes into the contract, rules on leakage, or produces a claim.

decisions.question: Who pays for the answers? A: the project holds one API key behind a proxy, with a per-visitor daily limit. B: each visitor brings their own key, nothing is stored server-side. C: A for a small free quota, then B.
decisions.context: A is the easiest for a fan but costs the project money and needs rate limiting and abuse handling. B costs nothing and has no abuse surface, but most casual fans will not have a key. C builds both paths. The CSP, App Check and the proxy design differ between A and B, so AI-06 cannot start before this is ruled. AI-07 measures cost per answer before AI-06 is needed, so the cap can be set from data. Recommendation revised 2026-10-15 from C to A for v1: C builds two paths before there is any usage data.
decisions.recommendation: A for v1, with a per-visitor daily limit and a hard daily spend cap sized from AI-07's cost per answer; add B later only if the cap binds.
decisions.resolution: Cloudflare Workers AI, on the account's free allowance (about 10,000 neurons a day) for now. The proxy is a Cloudflare Worker that calls Workers AI; the key/binding lives in the Worker, never the browser bundle. Firebase Hosting stays; the Worker is the only thing that touches the model API. Nothing else is decided (no paid tier, no bring-your-own-key path).

decisions.question: F9: laps the pipeline labels as a driver 'mistake' are dropped from training, and that label hangs on the tyre seed CO-02 is about to change. For v15: A: keep dropping them and delete the unused weight column (no change; the dependence on the seed stays). B: keep them at half weight (measured: no effect beyond noise; still tied to the seed). C: keep them at full weight (removes the dependence; quantile heads +1.3x the noise floor, cliff classifier -1.3x, all inside the 2x bar).
decisions.context: Measured 2026-10-10 in the fixes log (5 seeds, scratch warehouse): no arm clears the 2x reseed floor. Checked 2026-10-15: training_weight_f9 exists only in int_lap_anomaly_flags.sql:293; fct_cliff_prediction_features.sql:984 still excludes 'mistake' rows; nothing in ml/src reads the weight. The column also gives 1,234 event_driven rows a weight above 0, so B or C means fixing it first. Rides v15's retrain either way.
decisions.recommendation: C, because CO-02 rewrites the seed the 'mistake' label hangs on and C's costs and gains are both inside noise. A if you want the smallest possible v15.
decisions.resolution: A: keep dropping laps marked 'mistake'. F9 is closed as decided NOT WIRED. training_weight_f9 (int_lap_anomaly_flags.sql:293) is unused; deleting it is left to CO-03's rebuild, not done on 2026-10-15.

decisions.question: 2018 tyre-cliff cells: the point-in-time rule (FD3) fits each season only from earlier seasons, so 2018 has nothing to fit from, and every 2018 cell uses a hand-set default of 1.2-1.5 s, about twice what fitted cells show. What should 2018 (and any later cell with no usable fit) use? A: a declared prior: the median fitted value per compound class, labelled as a prior, not a fit. B: unknown (NULL): 2018 laps past a cliff onset get no label (about 42% of 2018 laps). C: fit 2018 on its own data, as a declared one-season exception to FD3.
decisions.context: Checked 2026-10-15: all 62 2018 rows of compound_cliff_params.csv equal the 09-28 seed and are class_default for onset and severity. The +0.37 s 2018 offset that compensated has been removed (dbt_project.yml:244 is {}), so 2018 ratings carry the over-correction again. A keeps 2018 in training with a small, declared class-level look-ahead. B follows FD6's 'NULL, not a guess' but drops most of 2018's post-cliff laps. C uses 2018's own data for its own label, which FD3 ruled against.
decisions.recommendation: A: honest about being a prior, keeps the 8-season training window whole, and lands close to what the fitted cells say.
decisions.resolution: C: fit 2018's cliff values on 2018's own data, as a declared one-season exception to FD3. Consequence: 2018 is then an in-sample fit. It must be labelled as such everywhere it appears and must never be used for any honest evaluation (validation, holdout, gates, headline metrics). Earlier-seasons-only (FD3) still applies to every other season.

decisions.question: Four improvements-board rulings have gone stale. D2 (deploy): the live CDN serves v14, the same as the local build, so 'production is on v6' no longer holds. A: close D2 as overtaken; the next publish question is v15, after CO-03. B: keep it open. D9 (may the pit-strategy cost curve read the ML predictions): its +3.59 s/stint and 33.9% -> 53.0% call reproduction were measured on v11 and the old seed. A: re-measure on v15 after CO-03, then rule. B: rule now on the principle. C: close as no. D13 (may an e-value its own item disowned be withdrawn before 04c's union run): A: yes, only when the same document disowned it for a stated computational reason (k* 5 -> 3). B: no, every declared E stands. D14 (does a label rebuild reopen 01b's noise floor; the label has been rebuilt twice since and CO-02 rebuilds it again): A: no; re-evaluate 01c's attainable block on the v15 label instead. B: yes, reopen 01b.
decisions.context: D2 checked 2026-10-15 against https://storage.googleapis.com/off-the-pace-cdn/models/manifest.json (model_version v14, built 2026-09-22). D9, D13 and D14 are unchanged in the improvements log since 2026-09-19/20. Answers are recorded there by CO-07; this entry is only the question as it stands today.
decisions.recommendation: D2 A, D9 A, D13 A, D14 A: each is the cheapest answer that stays honest, and none of them reopens settled work.
decisions.resolution: Yes to all four. D2: close (production already serves v14). D9: re-measure on v15 before any ruling; stays OPEN until then. D13: withdrawing a disowned e-value is allowed even where the original write-up rejected the idea. D14: do not reopen 01b's noise floor; recheck the newer attainable-block ceiling estimate on v15; stays OPEN until then. Recorded in the improvements log by CO-07.

watch_vocabulary.ship-blocker: Publishing or shipping without this breaks something users see. `board.py --ship` exits 1 while one is open.
watch_vocabulary.hazard: A standing trap that damages tracked files or results if someone does the obvious thing. Read before running anything nearby.
watch_vocabulary.uncommitted: Verified work that lives only in the working tree. Committing is the user's call.
watch_vocabulary.unreviewed: Changes in the working tree that no orchestrator has read or tested. Not to be built on until reviewed.
watch_vocabulary.unverified: A claim or code path that was run in one place only (dev but not CI, agent report but not re-run).
watch_vocabulary.stale-artifact: A built or generated thing that no longer matches the source it came from until it is rebuilt.
watch_vocabulary.pending-ruling: A question for the human that is not (yet) a blocking FD: it changes a note, a value or a scope, not an item's ability to run.
watch_vocabulary.gate-gap: A guard that does not guard: it errors, skips files silently, or cannot fail.
watch_vocabulary.debt: Known, documented, deliberately left. Each needs an owner eventually.

watch_model_vocabulary.haiku: Maps to haiku-4-5. A binary check, or recording a resolution the evidence or the user has already settled: is it committed, did the named tests pass on the rebuild, write down the accept. The output has a mechanical check (a test result, a file list, git log).
watch_model_vocabulary.sonnet: Maps to sonnet-5. The fix or the options are written down in the rule: pick between two named options, run a named rebuild or export and check the pages, review a diff, reconcile counts, reword text to a meaning already settled.
watch_model_vocabulary.opus: Maps to opus-5 (fable-5.1 if the rule turns into a new estimator). Rules on a trade-off, designs the fix, audits a decision, or turns a measurement into a claim: label-moving changes, leakage boundaries, gate runs before a promotion.
